zutable

zutable is a typed table for R: a data frame that knows each column’s type, queried through a bracket whose arguments are SQL’s clauses.

  • Every column has a logical type from Apache Arrow and a nullability, and a query’s result schema and type errors are known before any data is read.
  • := updates existing columns in place and never changes a table’s schema.
  • Grouping, sorting, joins and reductions run on a C kernel whose header other packages can use through LinkingTo.
  • It imports no other package; zufast, on CRAN, is needed only to build it, and pak installs it for you.

Installation

zutable is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zutable")

Usage

Build a table, then ask the bracket for the volume-weighted price of each id after the first day:

library(zutable)
trades <- zutable(
  id  = c(1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L),
  day = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:4,
  px  = c(10.5, 11, 20, 19.5, 7),
  qty = c(100L, 50L, 10L, 30L, 200L)
)
trades[where = day >= "2026-01-02",
       select = .(vwap = sum(px * qty) / sum(qty)),
       by = id]
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 2 columns
#>   id      vwap
#>   <int32> <float64>
#> 1 1       11.000
#> 2 2       19.625
#> 3 3       7.000

zutable also joins, updates in place, freezes and explains tables; Get started shows each.
